neighbours.label: the word just before a named geological or prehistoric period (the [last] ice age, during the [Pleistocene], the [Paleolithic])
fire: Woolly mammoths roamed the plains during the last ice age.
These valleys were carved by glaciers in the Pleistocene epoch.
Stone tools from the Paleolithic were found in the cave.
Sea levels were much lower at the height of the last glaciation.
The lake formed when ice retreated at the end of the Pleistocene.
Cave paintings date from the Upper Paleolithic period.
Much of Canada lay under ice during the last glacial maximum.
Fossils from the late Pliocene show early grazing animals.
quiet: Woolly sweaters were popular during the last winter sale.
These valleys were carved by rivers over many years.
Stone tools from the farm were found in the shed.
Sea levels were much lower at the time of the last survey.
The lake formed when the dam was finished at the end of the summer.
Cave paintings attract many tourists each summer.
Much of Canada lay under snow during the last cold snap.
Photos from the late afternoon show cattle grazing.

notes: Top examples: 'the'/'last' right before Ice Age, Pleistocene, Paleolithic, Pliocene. Logit effect of the + pole suppresses ' Ice', ' Ple', ' glac'. Near misses keep 'the last'/'during the' before non-geological nouns.
